subject: SLA validation / onboarding handshake: Beacon Health benchmark plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kumar <samir@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA validation / onboarding handshake: Beacon Health benchmark plan

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To make the handoff to implementation and keep your deadline for the pilot, I pulled together a concise benchmarking plan and proposed acceptance criteria so everyone has the same expectations. The goal here is to validate that the chosen model and config meet your latency p95 < 220ms for single-turn predictions and sustained throughput ~250 requests/sec for the ingestion pipeline under steady-state (90s windows).

Attached: benchmarking-checklist.xlsx (process + roles), initial-load-script.tar.gz (test harness).

Key items:
- Targets: p95 latency < 220ms; median latency < 80ms; sustained throughput 250 req/s (with 1k token average payload)
- Test windows: three 5-minute ramps: warmup, steady-state, and stress (burst to 500 req/s for 60s)
- Environment: dedicated staging cluster in us-west1 (match production GPU type: A10G), 4 workers, autoscaling disabled for the test run
- Metrics to capture: per-request latency histogram, token counts, CPU/GPU utilization, model KV cache hit rates, error rates (5xx/timeout)

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 3/23: dry run (small sample, config validation)
- Tue 3/24: formal benchmark (steady-state + burst)
- Wed 3/25: result review and signed acceptance or action items

Marissa, can you pick the lead for the customer success side and confirm the calendar invites? Dev, see "runbook" notes in the attached sheet for the few runtime knobs we think matter (batching, kv cache warm start).

Samir — if that looks reasonable I'll send invites and create a shared Drive folder for results.

Cheers,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
conner.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA validation / onboarding handshake: Beacon Health benchmark plan

Connor —

Appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications from our infra/ops folks:

1) We usually test from our eu-west region to validate cross-region performance. Can Redwood run an identical run from eu-west1 in addition to us-west1?
2) For throughput you call out 250 req/s with ~1k tokens avg — we'll validate payload distribution (we have a 75/25 split short/long messages). Should we provide a payload sample?
3) Who will own the failure playbook if the stress run exceeds error thresholds? Our SRE wants a contact and escalation path.

Also cc'd ops@beaconhealth.com (they will pick the test VM IPs).

Samir

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA validation / onboarding handshake: Beacon Health benchmark plan

Samir —

Thanks for the questions. A few technical clarifications from our infra team:

- We can run the identical harness from eu-west1. It's helpful if you can provide the payload distribution file (sample.json). We'll run two parallel runners pointing at the same model version to capture inter-region variance.
- For the stress-burst, we recommend keeping the client-side concurrency at 200 and use a short inter-request jitter to avoid artificial synchronization.
- Failure playbook: Redwood will own in-flight mitigation (circuit-breaker to fallback model variant + telemetry alerts). Beacon SRE will own IP whitelisting and VM-side diagnostics. Point-of-contact: dev_patel@redwood.com (pager: infra-oncall)

Operational knobs we plan to use during the run:
1) batch_size: 8 / 16 depending on token variance
2) kv cache warm-start: pre-warm with a 30s prefix load
3) token-limits: apply soft cap at 1,200 tokens to keep tail latencies bounded

I attached a quick results template and the runner config we'll execute.

– Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kumar <samir@beaconhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA validation / onboarding handshake: Beacon Health benchmark plan

Samir / team —

Thanks everyone for the runs. Summary of outcomes (formal run Tue 3/24 executed from us-west1 + eu-west1 as requested):

- Steady-state: us-west1 steady-state achieved 260 req/s with p95 = 205ms, median = 75ms; error rate = 0.4% (within threshold)
- eu-west1: steady-state 240 req/s with p95 = 235ms (missed target by ~15ms), median = 82ms; error rate = 0.6%
- Burst (500 req/s for 60s): both regions saw degradations; us-west degraded to p95 = 560ms with 2.4% 5xx; eu-west had p95 = 620ms and 3.1% 5xx

Artifacts uploaded to shared Drive: beam-results-20260322.csv (raw samples + histograms), Grafana snapshots, and a short run-report. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/shared/benchmark-plan-BEACON

Recommended next steps (joint items):
1) For eu-west p95 miss — try batch_size=16 and enable a 60s kv pre-warm on the runner. Dev will run a targeted iteration and report back by Tue 3/24 EOD PT.
2) For burst resiliency — propose a short-term SLA caveat: production fallback to a lower-capacity variant during extreme bursts and implement client-side rate smoothing. We'll draft language for the pilot SLA and send to Beacon procurement.
3) Action owners: Dev -> targeted eu-west tuning; Marissa -> draft pilot SLA language and run the acceptance checklist; Connor -> compile deck for 3/25 review.

Samir — please confirm if Beacon accepts the recommended next steps; if yes we'll treat the us-west run as accepted and list eu-west as "conditional acceptance" pending the tuning iteration.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
